## 1

You don’t have to decide tonight—maybe taking a day, checking your finances, or looking for another job first would give you more room to choose rather than escape under pressure. ## 2

I understand why some people are skeptical, especially when so much information online is manipulated or presented selectively. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on trusting a single space agency or photograph. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, see different stars from different latitudes, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, and compare time zones and flight routes. Independent scientists, private companies, and people who make their own observations all arrive at the same conclusion: Earth is approximately spherical, slightly flattened at the poles. The space photos are consistent with that broader body of evidence, rather than being the only reason to believe it.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s actually made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky.

That’s why the sky usually looks blue during the day. At sunset, sunlight has to travel through much more atmosphere. A lot of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches us, leaving more red, orange, and pink light visible.

雨落在深夜的城市里，像无数细小的手指，轻轻敲打着窗玻璃。街灯被水汽晕成一团朦胧的金黄，积水倒映着摇曳的树影和偶尔驶过的车灯。远处的屋檐不断滴水，声音清脆而有节奏。行人撑着伞匆匆走过，脚步溅起一圈圈涟漪。雨夜让喧闹的城市安静下来，也让孤独显得格外温柔。
